title: Take the brief, build the pieces and quote a job that pays

say: Take the brief, build the pieces, and quote a job that pays.
This is the video for module two of Event Decoration and Styling.
Most disputes start with words like elegant, or not too much, that mean different things to you and the client. A brief turns those words into written decisions.

panel.heading: Turn vague words into decisions
items: Event: date, times, when guests arrive
Venue: address, entry time, clear-out time
Guests, tables and table shape
Look: colours, aso ebi photos, likes, dislikes
Zones and budget for decor only
Rules: no nails, flames or confetti?

say: Ask about the event times and when guests arrive. Ask when you can enter the venue, and when you must clear out.

say: Ask the number of guests and tables. Ask for colours with photos of the aso ebi, three pictures they love, and one they dislike. One disliked picture can save you from a wrong direction.

say: Ask which zones to decorate, the budget for decor only, and the venue's rules. Then send a written summary back, measure the venue, and buy nothing until the client approves in writing.

say: Inflate 11 inch balloons slightly under full size, so they are rounder and less likely to burst. Use a sizer so they match.

say: Attach it to the stand with cable ties, then fill gaps with glue dots. Do not guess numbers. Build 30 cm, count, multiply by the length you need, and add about 10 percent for bursts.

say: Some guests are allergic to latex. For an indoor event with a known allergy, use foil balloons and fabric instead.

cards.d: Some guests are allergic to latex. With a known allergy indoors, use foil balloons and fabric.
Keep foil balloons away from overhead power lines. The metallic coating can conduct electricity.
Never hang fabric from light fittings, fans or cables. Use secure anchors, with the venue's permission.

say: And never hang fabric from light fittings, fans or electrical cables. If the hall has no safe fixing points, use free-standing frames.

say: For example, Grace has 12 round tables, each 60 inches across, and wants floor-length cloths.

panel.heading: The right tablecloth size
items: Table: 60 inches across
Floor-length drop: 30 inches
60 + 2 × 30 = 120 inch cloth
Order 13 for 12 tables: one spare

say: A standard table is about 30 inches high, so the drop is 30 inches on each side.

say: 60, plus two times 30, is 120. She needs 120 inch round cloths.

say: She orders 13, one spare in case of a stain. For backdrops, use about 1.5 to 2 times the frame width in fabric, so it gathers and looks full.

say: Many decorators work hard and still lose money because they price by feeling. Here is a quote that covers every naira. These prices are rough illustrations.
Materials she uses up, such as balloons and flowers, come to 86,000 naira. Rentals are 39,000.
She adds 10,000 for wear on her own pump and stands, so she can replace them.
Labour for her and 2 helpers, including pack-down, is 50,000. Transport is 20,000.
That is a subtotal of 205,000 naira.
Tolu adds 10 percent contingency for price changes and breakages. That makes 225,500.

panel.heading: Finish the quote, protect your money
items: Add 10 percent contingency: 225,500
Add 25 percent profit: quote 282,000
Deposit before you buy or rent
Balance before the event, not after
Payment counts only when it shows in your app

say: Then about 25 percent profit. She rounds her quote to 282,000 naira, with each zone listed.

say: Never buy or rent for a client without a deposit. Many decorators ask 50 to 70 percent on approval.

say: Collect the balance a few days before the event, and write your cancellation terms on the quote.

say: Accept a payment only when it shows in your own bank or wallet app. Screenshots can be faked. And if a client says it is too high, remove a zone or swap fresh flowers for artificial. Do not cut your profit.

panel.rule: Cut scope, not profit, when a client asks for less.

say: To remember. Get the brief and the approval in writing. Test-build your garland and count. Cloth equals table plus two times the drop. Quote every cost plus profit. Take a deposit first, and cut scope, not profit.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Written brief and approval before buying

Cloth = table + 2 × drop
Quote all six parts, plus profit
Deposit first; cut scope, not profit

say: Now run a practice brief with a friend and write a one-page proposal. Practise a garland, fabric gathers and a place setting at home. Then price a real job with deposit and cancellation terms.
